# Latchkey

> Your projects move; your secrets don't. Latchkey keeps API keys, database URLs and key files in iCloud Keychain;
> project files keep latchkey:// references; Latchkey fills the values in when a command starts, after the owner
> approves with Touch ID, Apple Watch or their password, or under a grant they made. For developers and the coding
> agents they run.

- Platform: macOS 15 or later (app); the command-line tool `latchkey` (`lk` for short) ships inside the app.
- Storage: iCloud Keychain, in Latchkey's own access group, synced to the owner's Macs. No Latchkey server or account.
- Install: the free download from GitHub releases, or `brew install --cask latchkey` after tapping
  zachshallbetter/latchkey. Latchkey Pro will be a one-time purchase in the Mac App Store version.
- Made by Snack Studio.

## For agents

- Run commands that need secrets as `latchkey run --env-file .env.local -- <command>` or
  `latchkey run --env <project>/<environment> -- <command>`.
- Never run `latchkey get`, never print the environment, never write values into .env files.
- Exit 77 means refused and 66 means missing: stop and ask the person; don't retry.
- `latchkey check` (or the MCP tool latchkey_check) shows what a run would get without asking.
- In a fresh clone or worktree: `latchkey project`, then `latchkey export <project>/<environment> --out .env.local`
  writes references from the environment's record (never values).
- Before committing, `latchkey scan --staged` lists env files that still hold plain values (names only); fix them
  with `latchkey import FILE --rewrite`.
- With `--proxy`, `--proxy-models A,B` and `--proxy-requests N` limit which models and how many requests a run may use.
- MCP: `latchkey mcp` serves latchkey_status, latchkey_list, latchkey_check, latchkey_run,
  latchkey_request_grant, latchkey_project and latchkey_export_references. It has no direct secret-read tool; child output masks exact values, but transformed secrets can leak.
